title: GLTF importer picks up -col and -convcol suffix on meshes, but ignores -colonly or -convcolonly on meshes
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in Godot v4.6.stable (89cea1439) ### System information Godot v4.6.stable (89cea1439) - macOS Sequoia (15.6.0) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M3 Ultra (Apple9) - Apple M3 Ultra (28 threads) - 96.00 GiB memory ### Issue description When importing scenes in GLTF format into Godot, if the **mesh name** contains a '-col' or '-convcol' suffix the appropriate collision mesh is generated when imported into Godot. However, if the **mesh name** contains a '-colonly' or '-convcolonly' suffix, the suffix is ignored by the importer and the mesh is treated as a regular visible mesh without collision. Note, this issue is specific to suffixes on the mesh name, not the node name, the latter work as expected. I noticed this issue while using geometry nodes to generate mesh instances in Blender. These don't give me control of node names for the instances but I can control their mesh names, or at least insert the appropriate suffix. However, the issue is not confined to geometry nodes and also happens on simple cases as shown in the repro example I've included below. For additional context, I've managed to fix this in a locally built copy of the Godot engine, but my fix is a workaround made with limited knowledge of the codebase, so I think it would be better for someone familiar with the code to address this rather than submitting a patch myself. * I found the location in editor/import/resource_importer_scene.cpp where these suffixes are handled. * The -col and -convcol suffixes for **node names** are handled around line 770 in the method ```ResourceImporterScene::_pre_fix_node()```. * Further down, there's an additional piece of _catch-all_ code that _also_ checks the **mesh name** for these suffixes, but there's nothing in place that does the same for -colonly and -convcolonly on the mesh name. ### Steps to reproduce ## Repro Steps If using the supplied MRP, please ignore steps 1 through 4. 1. Create a scene in Blender containing the default cube. 2. Name the mesh "Cube-col" 3. Duplicate the cube and name the mesh of the copy "Cube-colonly" 4. Export as GLTF and import into Godot. 5. Examine the scene graph by double clicking on the imported scene in Godot. 6. Notice that the first cube has a visible mesh and also a collision mesh, which is correct. 7. Notice that the 2nd cube has a visible mesh and no collision mesh, we would expect it to have a collision mesh and no visible mesh. ## Blender Scene Collection This shows the mesh names of the default cube and its duplicate. Note that the suffixes have been added to the meshes and not the node. ## Examining The Scene Graph in Godot 4.6 This shows that the default cube with a -col suffix on the mesh name has been interpreted as expected, but the duplicate with a -colonly suffix on the mesh name has not. ## Expected Result In Modified Engine This is the same scene loaded into my locally modified version of the engine. The duplicate mesh with the -colonly suffix now has collision geometry and lacks visible geometry as expected. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) ## MRP Open in Godot and double click on the "collision-bug-sample-scene.glb" in the filesystem pane to see the issue as described above. [collision-suffix-bug-example.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25075004/collision-suffix-bug-example.zip) ## Blender Scene I've included the .blend file for additional reference. [collision-bug-sample-scene.blend.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25075031/collision-bug-sample-scene.blend.zip)
